newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-NAB says no comment on St George stake.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-NAB says no comment on St George stake.

text.p: The National Australia Bank Ltd (NAB) declined on Friday to comment on its purchase of another one percent in Sydney-based St George Bank Ltd, saying only that its 7.79 percent stake was a strategic investment.
"We are not making any comment about the notice," NAB spokesman David Upton said, referring to NAB's announcement to the Stock Exchange on Thursday night of its increased stake.
"It's a strategic investment and that's all."
NAB moved in the Australian Stock Exchange on October 31 to increase its stake to 7.79 percent from 6.79 percent, but did not confirm this until after the market closed on Thursday.
The move comes as St George pursues a merger with its Sydney-based rival Advance Bank Australia Ltd.
NAB and at least one other major shareholder, National Mutual Holdings Ltd, have expressed unease that the merger will not be put to St George shareholders for approval.

Representatives of National Mutual's funds management arm met St George last week but the talks failed to resolve their concerns, said National Mutual Funds Management's Australian shares manager, Paul Jennings.
"We didn't make any progress," he told Reuters.
Asked if it was now clear little could be done to persuade St George to call a shareholders' meeting to consider the merger, he said: "I think that's probably right."
St George's scrip and cash bid values each Advance Bank share at A$7.30 -- nearly three times asset backing.
